banner.title: DEMIHUMANS AND DIVINE ASCENSION - DMO Chapter 7, round five of five: the demihuman advancement doctrine (retirement is what is supposed to happen, do not ignore the limits, the limits are the price of the demihuman advantages), the four solutions (a wish or 10th-level transformation spell to become human; a wish or 10th-level imbue spell per level beyond the racial maximum with the experience earned; the Slow Advancement rule with humans pulling ahead from 10th level; slow-after-max with the racial heroic task per extra level), the beyond-30th ceiling (all advancement stops at 30th, the pinnacle of mortal achievement, more hit points than five normal men, powers greater than the avatars), and the divine ascension path (seek anytime after 20th, never turn back, the divine sponsor, the gift at the experience-point total value, the 500,000-per-point saving throw benefit down to a minimum of three, the Table 59 offering roll with the three match columns, the heroic task with its five examples, no ability score under 13, the demigod-and-NPC ending, and the closing line: AD&D is a game of heroes, not gods).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 178-179 of the archive.org DMO captures (items dungeon-master-option-high-level-campaigns and tsr02156dmsoptionhighlevelcampaigns, the djvu.txt full texts; the tsr02156 ABBYY read is primary and the tesseract read is cross-checked; leaf N = printed page N). A prose-only round with no printed grids; both captures agree on every number. The only OCR artifact is the standing lOth-for-10th misread both captures make on the spell names (transformation, imbue), settled as 10th-level per the index and the standing OCR class. THE CHAPTER 7 PARENT flips with this round: every Chapter 7 child has now landed (R608 through R612).

consts.name: dfbSolutionCount
consts.comment: the demihuman solutions count: the DM can solve the demihuman advancement problem in four ways without forcing demihuman characters out of the game (printed p. 178).

consts.name: dfbImbueSpellsPerLevel
consts.comment: the second solution cost: each level gained beyond the maximum requires one wish or 10th-level imbue spell (printed p. 178).

consts.name: dfbSlowPullAheadLevel
consts.comment: the third solution note: at low levels slow advancement does not much affect play, but humans begin to pull ahead fairly rapidly once the characters reach 10th level or so (printed p. 178).

consts.name: dfbAdvancementStopsLevel
consts.comment: the mortal ceiling: all character advancement stops at 30th level, which represents the pinnacle of mortal achievement (printed p. 179).

consts.name: dfbAscendMinLevel
consts.comment: the ascension timing: a character can seek to ascend anytime after reaching 20th level, or earlier if the DM allows it (printed p. 179).

consts.name: dfbGiftMinValueXpRatio
consts.comment: the ascension offering floor: the gift monetary value must be at least equal to the character experience point total - the ratio is one copper or coin of value per experience point (printed p. 179).

consts.name: dfbSaveThrowXpStep
consts.comment: the ascension benefit: for each 500,000 experience points gained the character can lower one saving throw number one point (printed p. 179).

consts.name: dfbSaveThrowMin
consts.comment: the ascension benefit floor: the saving throw numbers go down to a minimum saving throw of three (printed p. 179).

consts.name: dfbTaskExampleCount
consts.comment: the ascension task examples: five sample heroic tasks are listed (printed p. 179).

consts.name: dfbMinAbilityScore
consts.comment: the ascension completion floor: the character cannot have any ability score or subability score lower than 13 (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbRetireIsIntended
bools.comment: the demihuman doctrine: demihuman characters are usually forced to retire or assume secondary roles once human characters reach high levels and the demihumans reach their advancement limits - that is exactly what is supposed to happen (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbDontIgnoreLimits
bools.comment: the demihuman doctrine: do not ignore demihuman advancement limits - many DMs are tempted to, especially when players are unwilling to retire their high-level demihuman characters (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbLimitsAreThePrice
bools.comment: the demihuman doctrine: the advancement limits are the price players must pay for gaining demihuman advantages at lower levels (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbIgnoringUnbalancesPlay
bools.comment: the demihuman doctrine: ignoring the advancement limits unbalances play by placing high-level power in the hands of characters who already have extra abilities (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbUnfairToHumanPlayers
bools.comment: the demihuman doctrine: ignoring the advancement limits is grossly unfair to players who chose human characters and labored to reach the point where their choices pay dividends in unlimited advancement (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbLimitsFactOfLife
bools.comment: the demihuman doctrine: demihuman advancement limits are a fact of life in any AD&D game world (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbSolutionWishTransformation
bools.comment: the first solution: a demihuman character can use a wish or 10th-level transformation spell to become human - the character might still look and act demihuman but has put aside the racial characteristics and special racial abilities that held the character back (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbSolutionWishImbue
bools.comment: the second solution: a demihuman character can use a wish or 10th-level imbue spell to gain one level beyond the normal racial maximum (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbImbueNeedsEarnedXp
bools.comment: the second solution gate: the character must have earned enough experience to actually gain the level (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbSolutionSlowAdvancement
bools.comment: the third solution: the DM can use the Slow Advancement rule from Chapter 2 of the Dungeon Master Guide (printed p. 178).

bools.name: dfbSolutionSlowOnlyAfterMax
bools.comment: the fourth solution: the DM can apply the Slow Advancement rule only after demihuman characters reach their maximum levels - representing their struggle to stay focused despite the distractions of being a demihuman (printed pp. 178-179).

bools.name: dfbRacialTaskPerExtraLevel
bools.comment: the fourth solution doctrine: reflect the demihuman nonhuman viewpoint by requiring a heroic task that furthers the interests of the character race each time the character advances a level beyond the usual maximum (printed pp. 178-179).

bools.name: dfbRacialHeroExample
bools.comment: the fourth solution example: an elf wizard might undertake a quest to protect a tract of virgin forest and perhaps establish a colony there - this kind of effort marks the character as a racial hero instead of a demihuman with human interests (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbWizardMoreHpThanFiveMen
bools.comment: the 30th-level note: at this level even a wizard has more hit points than five normal men (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbPowersExceedAvatars
bools.comment: the 30th-level note: characters of any class have powers greater than the avatars that deities use to conduct business in the mortal world (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbNowhereElseToGo
bools.comment: the 30th-level note: once a character has gotten this far there is nowhere else to go - or is there? (the printed hook into divine ascension) (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbNeedsDmApproval
bools.comment: the ascension gate: with the DM approval a character can abandon his or her profession and follow a different path to power - divine ascension requires a great deal of attention and creativity from both DM and player, and only the barest guidelines are given because each character and campaign are unique (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbOnlyOptionAfter30
bools.comment: the ascension timing: once a character has reached 30th level this is the only option that allows the character any further advancement (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbNeverTurnBack
bools.comment: the ascension doctrine: once the character embarks on the path to godhood he can never turn back (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbCeasesClassAdvancement
bools.comment: the ascension doctrine: the character ceases advancing in the original class (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbRetainsClassAbilities
bools.comment: the ascension doctrine: the character retains all class abilities but gives up normal adventuring and acts with a new purpose (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbNeedsDivineSponsor
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: the character must seek a divine sponsor - usually a deity appropriate to the character alignment, original class and race - and prepare a special offering for that deity (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbGiftDmAgreed
bools.comment: the ascension offering: the gift can be anything the character desires and the DM agrees to, and the donation need not be a single item (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbXpNormalDuringPreparation
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: while preparing the offering the character receives experience points normally (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbBelowClassMinimumSpecial
bools.comment: the ascension doctrine: the ability to reduce saving throw numbers below the normal minimum for the character original class is special, and it is why the character must give up the original class (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbNoOtherXpBenefits
bools.comment: the ascension doctrine: the character gains no other benefits from accumulated experience - no hit points, proficiencies, skills, etc. (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbJourneyToAbode
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: when the offering is completed the character must journey to the deity abode and present the gift (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTrueCharactersLikelyAccepted
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: if the character has been true to the principles of alignment and profession the deity probably accepts the gift (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTable59ReactionRoll
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: if in doubt use Table 59 Encounter Reactions from the Dungeon Master Guide - matching deity alignment and portfolio use the first column, a slight mismatch the second, otherwise the third (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbFriendlyAccepts
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: if the reaction roll is friendly the deity accepts the gift (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbUnfriendlyDestroysGift
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: if not, the deity destroys the gift and sends the character away - the character can try again with the same deity or with another deity (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbMaybeNoImmediateAudience
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: the character might not get an immediate audience - just finding and entering the deity abode could be an adventure in itself, and the Planescape setting material can provide details (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbDeityAssignsTask
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: once the deity accepts the gift it assigns some heroic task to the character, and completing the task proves the character mettle - in a Planescape campaign the character becomes the deity proxy (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTaskExampleDynasty
bools.comment: the first task example: found a dynasty (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTaskExampleCreation
bools.comment: the second task example: create a new magical item or spell that others seek to imitate (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTaskExampleArtifact
bools.comment: the third task example: find and destroy an artifact from an opposing alignment (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTaskExampleRivalAvatar
bools.comment: the fourth task example: find and defeat the avatar of a rival deity (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTaskExampleMonument
bools.comment: the fifth task example: build a lasting monument to the deity (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbDmDesignsTaskAdventures
bools.comment: the ascension procedure: it is up to the DM to create a suitable task and design a series of adventures so the character can complete it (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbTaskNeedsAllSavesAtThree
bools.comment: the ascension completion: the character must complete the task and earn enough experience to lower all saving throw numbers to three (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbBecomesDemigod
bools.comment: the ascension completion: when all of that is accomplished the character becomes a demigod and companion to the sponsor - and the character becomes an NPC under the DM control (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbPlayersMayBeUpset
bools.comment: the ascension epilogue: some players may be upset that they have worked hard only to lose control of their characters - remind them of their contributions to the campaign world (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbNewCharactersWorshipHeroes
bools.comment: the ascension epilogue: new characters can worship their retired heroes and demigods, and the players should be invited to help construct the new powers portfolios (printed p. 179).

bools.name: dfbHeroesNotGods
bools.comment: the ascension epilogue, pinned verbatim: AD&D is a game of heroes, not gods (printed p. 179).

table_checks.expr: m['dfbSaveThrowXpStep']() != 500000 or m['dfbSaveThrowMin']() != 3 or m['dfbAscendMinLevel']() != 20 or m['dfbGiftMinValueXpRatio']() != 1
